article.title: Trump Denied Project 2025
article.author: Ted Vaill
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. By February, 2026, 53% of the goals of “Project 2025” had been initiated or accomplished by Trump and his gang, or 283 out of 532 recommended actions in this Heritage Foundation document that Trump claimed he had nothing to do with. However, the key authors of this document comprised 70% of Trump’s cabinet members, and over 50 of Trump’s senior government officials had direct ties to Project 2025. Over 140 of Trump appointees helped write Project 2025, including Russ Vought, director of Trump’s Office of Management and Budget, Steve Miller, his Deputy Chief of Staff, and Brendon Carr, head of the FCC. Other authors include Rick Dearborn, Christopher Miller, Ken Cuccinelli, Dr. Ben Carson, Peter Navarro, and Edwin Feulner, the co-founder and former President of the Heritage Foundation . The Heritage Foundation was formed in 1973, and became a leading conservative think tank. In recent years, it has shifted its positions on a number issues. They now support: opposing aid to Ukraine, embracing “Trumpism”, doubting election results, supporting significant reductions in the federal workforce and weakening career civil servants’ influence, avoring the U.S. retreating from international foreign policy alignments, opposing “Communists” and “Socialists” in government, *admiring some of the tactics of Joe McCarthy, and*supporting the unitary executive theory. Related: Are We On the Verge of a Revolution? The “unitary executive theory”, championed by Edwin Feulner, Steve Bannon and Steve Miller, lays out a blueprint for an unprecedented expansion of executive powers and “deconstruction of the administrative state”, as Bannon calls it. In 2019, Trump declared that “I have the right to do whatever I want as President”. The theory posits that the President should have sole control over the executive branch. However, past experience in Hungary, Poland and Turkey have shown how centralizing executive power can undermine the rule of law, skew election results, and shrink dissent, increasing the decline of democracy. Implemented Project 2025 objectives by Trump and his cronies have already centralized executive authority and reduced regulatory oversight and undermined our democracy. A past example: the George W. Bush deregulation led up to the 2008 financial crisis, which emboldened corporate misconduct leading to financial abuses and market failures. In the future, the failure to regulate AI could lead to the destruction of civilization. Trump wants the AI industry to control itself, not the government. Related: Time's Up? What to do? Trump has started an unpopular war with Iran, imposed unwise tariffs, and increased by a lot the cost of living for Americans, and he does not care, as he lives in his self- promoting bubble. He looks unwell, and may be inflicted with the dementia that killed his father. Many of the polls show that on November 3 there will be a gigantic blue wave that will return the Democrats to power in the House and Senate. However, if this fails to happen, or if Trump attempts a 1/6-type coup by messing with the Midterms, the only response would be to capitulate to a Trump autocracy or have a civil war. Trump and his billionaires are throwing millions at the Midterm elections to convince voters that the Republicans should stay in power in Congress and throughout the country. If the American voters buy into this Trump and GOP bullshit, all is lost. We will have two more years of Trump’s unitary executive power, and the likely end of our democracy.
